chunk_findings.detail: `dirs = os.pathsep.join(...)` on an empty `extra_dirs` tuple yields `""`. Passing `path=""` to `shutil.which` makes Python’s implementation treat the empty component as `os.curdir` and search the current working directory. Thus `select(extra_dirs=())` can return an executable named `opencode`/`kilo` from the current directory even though no extra directory was requested; it should search only `PATH` in that call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/opencode.py:select

chunk_findings.detail: When the template is rendered with `item` unset or empty (which the template explicitly anticipates with `{% if item %}`), the rendered text still says: “Work only inside ... and only on files the item's lease allows.” In that input there is no item and no item lease, so the instruction is self-contradictory: the worker is told to respect a lease that does not exist, and may either ignore the constraint or infer that no files are allowed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/harness/opencode/instructions.md.j2:5

chunk_findings.detail: The generated lane instructions omit the required end-of-run/phase/compaction ddflow self-assessment step from [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `seen["cwd"] == str(wt)` compares the child process's `os.getcwd()` (which the POSIX `getcwd()` call canonicalizes by resolving symlinks) with `str(wt)` as returned by `tmp_path` without canonicalization. On macOS, `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`, so a path like `/var/folders/.../repo` comes back from `os.getcwd()` as `/private/var/folders/.../repo`; the test then fails in that environment even though the lane correctly launched in the intended directory.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_opencode.py:test_lane_runs_headless_in_the_worktree_with_private_home

chunk_findings.detail: `select` returns the result of `shutil.which` exactly as found, without normalizing it to an absolute path. If `opencode`/`kilo` is discovered through a relative `PATH` entry (for example `PATH=bin:/usr/bin` with an executable `bin/opencode` in the current directory), `_version` succeeds because it runs before the cwd changes, but `prepare` later passes that relative `Binary.path` into `argv_for` and sets `LaunchSpec(cwd=str(worktree))`. The launch then tries to execute `<worktree>/bin/opencode`, which does not exist, so the lane cannot start even though a working binary was selected and version-read.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/opencode.py:select

chunk_findings.detail: The `tree` fixture writes the `.ddflow/` ignore rule to the main checkout's `.git/info/exclude`, but the later `git status --porcelain` assertion runs inside the linked worktree `wt` created at line 77. For a linked worktree, Git reads `${GIT_DIR}/info/exclude` from `.git/worktrees/lane/info/exclude`, not the main `.git/info/exclude`. Therefore any `.ddflow/` file written by `OC.prepare` under `wt` (the reason this ignore rule exists) is reported as untracked, so `assert sh(wt, "git", "status", "--porcelain").stdout == ""` fails.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_opencode.py:72

chunk_findings.detail: `FAKE` builds the shebang as `#!{py}` with `sys.executable` across `fake_bin`. In a POSIX environment where `sys.executable` contains a space, e.g. `/opt/My Python/bin/python`, the kernel parses the shebang as interpreter `/opt/My` with optional argument `Python/bin/python`, so executing the generated fake binary fails with `ENOENT`. Every test that calls `fake_bin` would then fail before producing version output or lane events.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_opencode.py:31

chunk_findings.detail: `select` documents `DDFLOW_<NAME>_BIN` as “an executable path”, but it resolves the overridden value with `which(override)`. `shutil.which` does not expand `~`, and for a value such as `DDFLOW_OPENCODE_BIN=[REDACTED:path]` it checks `$PWD/[REDACTED:path]`; for a bare name it searches `PATH`. Concrete failure: with `DDFLOW_OPENCODE_BIN=[REDACTED:path]` in `/tmp` and `/usr/local/bin/opencode` on `PATH`, `which("[REDACTED:path]")` returns `None`, so the function falls back to `/usr/local/bin/opencode` and silently runs a different binary than the configured executable path. The override should be handled as a path (expanding `~` and checking that exact file), or the code/documentation should not claim it accepts an executable path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/opencode.py:select

chunk_findings.detail: The new self-assessment instruction still does not satisfy [r-ddflow-self-assessment]. The rule requires an assessment at the end of every agent run, at every phase, and before context compaction, and requires checking both that a defect is not duplicated and not already corrected. The added line only triggers “When your run ends” and only says “after checking it is not already filed.” A lane worker that passes through multiple phases or compacts context will not be told to assess ddflow at those required checkpoints, and may file a defect that is already corrected because that check is omitted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/harness/opencode/instructions.md.j2:10

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test calls `OC.select(extra_dirs=())` without passing an explicit `environ`, so `OC.select` reads the real process environment. The test clears `PATH` and changes the current directory, but it does not clear `DDFLOW_OPENCODE_BIN`. If that variable is set in the environment (for example, a developer or CI configuration that points to a specific opencode binary), `OC.select` will honor the override and return an `OC.Binary`, so the assertion `isinstance(OC.select(extra_dirs=()), ld.Result)` fails even when the cwd-search bug is actually fixed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_opencode.py:test_select_with_no_extra_dirs_never_searches_cwd

The same mapping is used to read `DDFLOW_OPENCODE_BIN`, so an explicit environment gives inconsistent expansion: with `environ={"DDFLOW_OPENCODE_BIN": "[REDACTED:path]", "HOME": "/tmp/lane-home"}` and process `HOME=[REDACTED:path]`, the code checks `[REDACTED:path]` instead of `/tmp/lane-home/bin/opencode` and may then fall back to a different `opencode` on `PATH`. The new tilde support is therefore wrong for the explicit-`environ` input path the function accepts.
